title: Implementation, Ad-hoc & Constructive (Depth Pass)
relevance: High — second ladder for post-basics CF fluency: the “any valid construction / find the invariant” skill that separates green from cyan–blue in contests and still shows up as OA twist questions.
company_notes: Google/Meta phone screens: construct any array/string under constraints (Game-With-Array or Balance-the-Bits — existence check + simple builder). Amazon OA variants: prefix-sum/cut “split so no subarray sums to 0” ≡ Non-zero Segments. Microsoft-style scheduling/load balance: Phoenix and Towers / Grid-00100 — next job to lightest bin. Harder onsite graph twists: Coloring Edges-style 1 or 2 labels depending on cycles.

phases.goal: Spot constructive/ad-hoc depth problems that ask for any valid object, a short sequence, or an impossibility proof rather than a heavy algorithm.

must_hit.point: Statement cues are “construct any”, “minimum length sequence”, or “prove impossible”; constraints usually allow O(n log n) or O(n·alphabet), not heavy algorithms.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate names those phrasing cues and says fancy DS is usually unnecessary under the stated complexity band.

must_hit.point: You win by discovering a small certificate — parity, first vs last, max frequency gap, degree ≥ 3 vertex, or Hamming-1 candidate — not by simulating a complex process first.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists certificate examples like first-vs-last, parity, max-frequency gap, or a high-degree vertex before proposing code.

must_hit.point: Classic OA/interview shapes include Game-With-Array / Balance-the-Bits existence+builder, Non-zero Segments prefix cuts, and lightest-bin assignment (Phoenix and Towers / Grid-00100).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maps the prompt to one of those named patterns: half-sum dodge, double RBS from a mask, prefix-set cuts, or always assign to shortest tower.

probes: What in the statement tells you this is a constructive/ad-hoc problem rather than a DP or graph-algorithm problem?
Which small invariant or certificate would you hunt for before writing any builder?

hints.1: Look at the ask: any valid object, shortest sequence, or prove impossible.
hints.2: Constraints and phrasing usually point to O(n log n) / O(n·alphabet) builders driven by a tiny certificate.
hints.3: Name certificates like parity, first vs last, max frequency, degree ≥ 3, or Hamming-1 and match to Game-With-Array, Non-zero Segments, or lightest-bin scheduling.

phases.goal: Turn the certificate into a canonical skeleton construction and know when to rephrase reversible ops instead of simulating them.

must_hit.point: After the certificate, build the simplest object that meets it — zig-zag permutations, powers-of-two arrays, two RBS from a 0/1 mask, MEX placements, or difference-array rewrites.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Picks a named skeleton (zig-zag, powers of two, twin RBS, MEX loop, diff-array) tied to the certificate.

must_hit.point: Prefer canonical skeletons from the checklist: all-1s + leftover, powers of two, zig-zag permute, wrapped diagonals, two RBS twins.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explicitly prefers one of those skeletons over an ad-hoc search or full simulation.

must_hit.point: When ops are reversible, rephrase as reach sorted / zero / equal and count the rewritten form; don’t simulate each op.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says to rewrite the ops (e.g. difference-array / gather-then-redistribute) and argue reachability instead of stepping every update.

must_hit.point: Tree/path label problems: concentrate extreme labels on a high-degree or endpoint edge set (e.g. put 0,1,2 on edges of a deg≥3 vertex).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions concentrating small labels on a deg≥3 vertex’s edges, or path ends if none exists.

probes: Once you have the invariant, what is the simplest object you would actually emit?
If the operations are reversible, how do you rephrase the goal before coding?

hints.1: Don’t start by simulating; name the certificate first.
hints.2: Match certificate → skeleton: all-1s+leftover, powers of two, zig-zag, wrapped diagonals, twin RBS, MEX placement, diff-array.
hints.3: For trees, put 0,1,2 on a deg≥3 vertex’s edges; for reversible ops, rewrite to sorted/zero/equal and count that form.

phases.goal: Show concrete builders for the core constructions and the important case splits the ladder trains.

must_hit.point: “No subset sums to S/2” → dump almost-all 1s and one big leftover (Game With Array), with OA-style case split on S≥2N.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes nearly all 1s plus one leftover and mentions the S≥2N case split.

must_hit.point: Prefix-sum collision → insert a cut / reset the running sum set (Non-zero Segments).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maintains a set of seen prefixes and on a repeat cuts and restarts the set.

must_hit.point: Balance the Bits: two bracket strings from a 0/1 mask using parity of zeros plus leading/trailing ones; Bracket Coloring colors by sign of balance with 1 vs 2 colors from global regularity.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explains mask→two RBS with zero-parity and end ones, or coloring by balance sign with a 1-vs-2 regularity check.

must_hit.point: Ehab the Xorcist: XOR+sum reconstruct with length ≤ 3 always via cases on u⊕s and bit carries; Special Permutation builds consecutive diffs in {2,3,4} and is impossible for n≤3.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Caseworks length 1/2/3 for XOR+sum, or builds diffs in {2,3,4} and rejects n≤3.

must_hit.point: Make Them Equal: ops move mass in multiples of indices — gather then redistribute; impossible if sum ∤ n. Matrix fills check n·a = m·b and use cyclic shifts / wrapped diagonals so row/col loads differ by at most one.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States gather-to-index-1 then redistribute multiples of i with the divisibility check, or cites n·a = m·b before cyclic/diagonal placement.

probes: Walk through how you would construct an array so no subset sums to half the total.
How do you place cuts so no subarray sum is zero using prefix sums?

hints.1: Pick one core builder: half-sum dodge, prefix cuts, or twin RBS.
hints.2: Game With Array ≈ almost-all 1s + leftover with S≥2N; Non-zero Segments ≈ seen-prefix set + cut on repeat.
hints.3: Also mention XOR+sum length ≤ 3 casework, diffs in {2,3,4} with n≤3 impossible, or gather/redistribute when sum ∤ n blocks.

phases.goal: Anchor expected runtime in the constructive band and the light structures these solutions use.

must_hit.point: Constraints usually allow O(n log n) or O(n·alphabet), not heavy algorithms.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States the solution should fit O(n log n) or O(n·alphabet) rather than advanced algo machinery.

must_hit.point: The “DS” of constructive here is prefix-sum sets, difference arrays, and MEX-placement loops — plus set/heap for always assigning to the current shortest tower.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names prefix-sum sets, diff arrays, MEX loops, and optionally a heap/set for lightest-tower assignment.

must_hit.point: Sage's Birthday-style zig-zag may binary-search the count of local minima, but the interleaving construction itself is the core; Replace by MEX sorts via ≤2n MEX placements.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions optional binary search on zig-zag count and/or a ≤2n MEX-placement bound for sorting.

probes: What time bound should your construction target on typical CF/OA constraints for these problems?
Which lightweight structures replace a “real” heavy DS here?

hints.1: Think linearithmic or linear in n times alphabet, not flow/segtree-heavy.
hints.2: Prefix-sum sets, difference arrays, MEX loops, and a heap for shortest tower are enough.
hints.3: Quote O(n log n) or O(n·alphabet); mention ≤2n MEX placements or optional binary search only as stretch detail.

phases.goal: Catch the edge cases and false starts the depth ladder repeatedly punishes.

must_hit.point: Always hunt an invariant/certificate before coding a simulation — Element Extermination reduces to a[1] < a[n] (“simulate mentally, not literally”).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Refuses blind simulation and cites a first-vs-last style check such as a[1] < a[n].

must_hit.point: Binary String Reconstruction needs care on the n1=0 edge; Omkar and Baseball answers only 0/1/2 from the single unsorted contiguous segment pattern.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Calls out n1=0 stitching and the 0/1/2 segment trichotomy.

must_hit.point: Make Them Equal is impossible if sum ∤ n; Special Permutation is impossible for n≤3; A/B Matrix needs n·a = m·b before building.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States the divisibility/existence guards before describing any construction.

must_hit.point: Coloring Edges: 1 color if DAG, else 2 (back-edge vs tree-edge by DFS timestamp) — chromatic number of conflict is 1 or 2 by directed-cycle parity; do not over-color.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says 1 color on a DAG and 2 otherwise via DFS back-edge vs tree-edge, tied to directed-cycle parity.

probes: What goes wrong if you simulate Element Extermination instead of finding the invariant?
Which impossibility checks must you run before emitting a construction?

hints.1: Name one brittle edge: n1=0, n≤3, or sum not divisible by n.
hints.2: Invariant-first: a[1] < a[n], single unsorted segment → 0/1/2, existence equalities before matrix fill.
hints.3: Also: DAG → 1 color else 2 by DFS timestamps; don’t invent more colors than the cycle-parity argument needs.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: For problems like Element Extermination, reduce to a certificate such as a[1] < a[n] and reason about the process mentally; coding a full simulation is slower and obscures the real condition.

Prefer fixed skeletons (all-1s + leftover, nearest powers of two under a sum bound, zig-zag interleaving, wrapped diagonals, twin RBS) once the certificate is known; searching for any feasible object is unnecessary when a standard builder is complete.

tradeoffs.topic: Rewrite reversible ops vs simulate each update
tradeoffs.strong_answer: When ops are reversible (difference-array range fixes, index-multiple mass moves), rephrase as reaching sorted/zero/equal and count or construct the rewritten form; per-op simulation hides impossibility checks like sum ∤ n.

tradeoffs.topic: Direct zig-zag count vs binary-searching the answer
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Sage's Birthday maximizes local minima by small/large interleaving; binary-searching the count is optional — the interleaving construction is the core.

Coloring Edges needs 1 color iff the digraph is a DAG, else 2 via back-edge vs tree-edge; Edge Weight Assignment uses leaf-parity for min colors 1 or 3 and a max from n−1 minus extra leaf edges at the same vertex — pick the theorem-shaped case split instead of a general chromatic solver.

gotchas.trap: Building a Binary String from (n0,n1,n2) without handling n1=0.
gotchas.correction: Stitch runs from the pair counts carefully; the n1=0 edge is a special case called out on the ladder.

gotchas.trap: Assuming a Special Permutation with consecutive diffs in {2,3,4} exists for every n.
gotchas.correction: Impossibility for n≤3; only build that diff set when n is large enough.

gotchas.trap: Redistributing with Make Them Equal ops without checking total sum.
gotchas.correction: Impossible if sum ∤ n; otherwise gather total sum to index 1, then redistribute multiples of i.

gotchas.trap: Forgetting Game With Array’s case split when forcing no subset sum equal to S/2.
gotchas.correction: Use almost-all 1s and one big leftover, with the OA-style case split on S≥2N.

gotchas.trap: Balance the Bits from a 0/1 mask without end/parity constraints.
gotchas.correction: Two RBS strings need the parity of zeros plus leading/trailing ones conditions.

gotchas.trap: Path-etic MEX labeling without using a high-degree vertex.
gotchas.correction: Put 0,1,2 on edges of a deg≥3 vertex; if none, use path ends — that maximises path MEXs.
1 color if DAG, else 2 (back-edge vs tree-edge by DFS timestamp); conflict chromatic number is 1 or 2 by directed-cycle parity.

gotchas.trap: Starting matrix construction before the global balance check.
gotchas.correction: For A/B Matrix, existence requires n·a = m·b; then use cyclic column shifts (or wrapped diagonals in Grid-00100) so loads differ by ≤1.
